steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Greeks worshipped the twelve Olympian gods, each with specific domains: Zeus (king of gods), Hera (marriage), Athena (wisdom), Apollo (prophecy/music), Poseidon (sea), Ares (war), Aphrodite (love), etc. | Key Fact: Sacrifice (thusia) was the central act of Greek worship: animal sacrifices were offered at temples and altars, with the gods receiving the bones and fat while worshippers ate the meat | Key Fact: Oracles, especially Delphi (sacred to Apollo), provided divine guidance on major decisions: war, colonisation, politics | Key Fact: Pan-Hellenic festivals (Olympic, Pythian, Nemean, Isthmian Games) brought Greeks together in celebration and athletic competition

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from greek religion &amp; culture, and one past-paper question.
